**Conversation Overview**

The person is an experienced player of Absolum (a beat 'em up roguelite by Dotemu, released October 2025) who came to Claude seeking help locating a secret dragon fight in the game. They had previously fought the dragon with another player but didn't know how to get there themselves. Over the course of the conversation, the person demonstrated deep, firsthand knowledge of the game's mechanics — often more accurate than what Claude found through web searches — and frequently corrected Claude's terminology and assumptions when they diverged from actual in-game reality.

The conversation covered several topics: finding the Hagen the Spectral Doom secret dragon fight (beach skeleton triggered by thumbs-down gesture), locating the gesture input mechanic on controller (hold LB + direction), the game's procedurally structured region/scene system (regions as map symbols with 2–6 shifting scenes each, fixed encounters with prerequisites), and a lengthy exploration of hub-area NPC physics the person discovered in real time — including that babies, the ghost from the library/mountain door, and some anchored NPCs respond differently to gestures and have push physics. The person also shared detailed knowledge of the Ordeal system (post-game corruption modifiers), the crystal farming loop using stacked enemy-count/aggression Ordeals with lifesteal assists, and the hidden trinket upgrade room beneath the training dummy platform with its exponential shared-price-doubling mechanic across three zones. The person's stated goal is to farm an extremely large crystal stockpile to max out all trinkets across all zones before going into online multiplayer, where they intend to host sessions for other players. Claude flagged uncertainty about whether guests in a hosted session share the host's crystal pool, searched for clarification, and surfaced that the session appears to sync to the lower-progress player's state rather than granting guest access to the host's resources — which the person had not yet verified in-game.

Several important corrections the person made to Claude's approach are worth preserving: "hub" in this game refers to the death-respawn home base (not a central area), the goblin path is a player-chosen branch not a randomly assigned route, regions are the correct unit of map structure (not "paths"), beach scenes are variable within the beach region rather than the beach region itself being variable, and the person confirmed babies can be found as any character (contradicting one forum source Claude cited). The person also pointed out that Claude could have searched developer changelogs or official patch notes as a primary source rather than relying solely on player-written guides — a more reliable approach when game mechanics are ambiguous across secondhand sources. The person communicates casually and humorously, appreciated directness when Claude acknowledged uncertainty rather than fabricating answers, and was clear that they wanted real sourced information rather than plausible-sounding guesses.

- Break the brambles/bushes at the bottom-right of one of the starting screens in that frog village area, then jump into the pond behind it.
